clue.text: Witch's spell is proof against tears

parts.note: something proof against a force cannot be harmed by it, so it can't (CANT without the apostrophe)
tears as a verb means rips

explanation.surface: A magic charm guarantees that something will never be torn.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'tears' as rips, not weeping: what is proof against tearing CAN'T RIP. A cantrip is a Scots word for a witch's spell or trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrip is a Scottish term for a magic charm or piece of witchcraft.

clue.text: Sweet heliotrope

definitions.meaning: a dessert or pudding made with red fruit in pastry
a garden plant with fragrant purple flowers, popularly named after the fruit tart because of its scent

explanation.definitionFit: The dessert of fruit baked in pastry shares its name with heliotrope, whose flowers smell of it.

clue.text: Lower one inside? Not one nor t'other

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes inside the word for lower

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Should the lower one go inside? Neither option appeals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not either of two, rejecting both alternatives.

clue.text: Gladiator semi-retiring to island state in USA perhaps

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the word retiring is kept
the island state's abbreviation sits in the rearranged letters
perhaps shows the letters might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation of Rhode Island, the US state named as an island

explanation.surface: A gladiator half-retires to Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-' keeps RETI, half of 'retiring'; 'perhaps' turns USA into AUS, and 'in' puts RI inside to make ARIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiarius was a Roman net-fighter, a gladiator armed with net and trident.

clue.text: See, climbing up, many a mountain lion

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the word up is reversed

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Look, a mountain lion climbing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just points the solver to the instruction; 'climbing' reverses UP to PU, then M (a thousand) and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Puma is another name for the cougar, the large wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Monkey breaks section of balcony wall

indicators.note: the monkey breaks into the section, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a section is a part
an ape is a kind of monkey in loose usage

explanation.surface: A monkey smashes part of a balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is the low protective wall along the edge of a balcony, roof or bridge.

clue.text: Father perhaps holding post up in Westminster.

indicators.note: the father holds the post, so it sits inside him

parts.note: a father is an example of a parent

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: post means mail

explanation.surface: A dad, perhaps, carrying a signpost in Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MAIL into LIAM, which 'holding' places inside PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster is the London seat of the UK legislature and is used as shorthand for it.

clue.text: Bad lad, but topping Irish accent

indicators.note: topping means removing the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish accent

explanation.surface: A naughty boy who nonetheless has a terrific Irish accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like the slang for excellent; it means cutting off the top, B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a mischievous or dishonest fellow, a rascal.

clue.text: Court attendant, a six-footer, in historical procession

parts.note: a page is a boy servant at a royal court
an ant, like any insect, has six legs

explanation.surface: A court servant, a very tall one, marches in a costume parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a colourful public show or parade re-enacting scenes from history.

clue.text: Territorial award includes little material

indicators.note: the award includes the small word, holding it inside

parts.note: TD is the Territorial Decoration, awarded to officers of Britain's Territorial Army reserve
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A medal for volunteer soldiers comes with a small piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: TD, the Territorial Decoration, is a British medal for long service in the volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, originally woven in Scotland.

clue.text: George as novelist succeeded by this poet

definitions.meaning: Mary Ann Evans wrote Middlemarch under the pen name George plus this surname
T. S. of The Waste Land shares the novelist's surname

explanation.surface: A novelist named George is followed by a poet of the same name.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Victorian novelist George and modernist poet T. S. bear the surname; the poet came later, hence 'succeeded by'.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is shared by the novelist who wrote Middlemarch and the poet who wrote The Waste Land.

clue.text: One enjoying the security of a home perhaps

definitions.text: One enjoying the security of a home perhaps

parts.words: One enjoying the security of a home perhaps
parts.note: not a homeowner feeling safe but a lender who holds the house as security for a loan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Security' suggests feeling safe at home; here it is the financial sense, the property pledged against a loan, which the lender holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The lender in a home loan holds a legal claim on the property as collateral until the debt is repaid.

clue.text: Warm up again for first race about to start

indicators.note: the word for about is placed at the start, before the race

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a heat is a preliminary race

explanation.surface: Getting warmed up again for the opening race, which is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to start' reads as one phrase meaning imminent; split it, so 'about' gives RE and 'to start' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat food or a room is to make it hot once more.

clue.text: Any drive winding to Martha's place in USA

indicators.note: a winding road twists, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Any road you take twists its way to Martha's house in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Martha's Vineyard is an island resort off Massachusetts; 'Martha' is not a person here.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is a well-known island off the coast of Massachusetts.

clue.text: Bubble-blowing victim of a nine a.m. drowning

definitions.text: Bubble-blowing victim of a nine a.m. drowning

parts.words: Bubble-blowing victim of a nine a.m. drowning
parts.note: in the folk song, the miner's daughter drove ducklings to the water every morning at nine and fell into the foaming brine

explanation.walkthrough: The American folk song 'Oh My Darling' tells of a girl who led ducklings to the water at nine each morning, fell in, and sank blowing bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The miner's daughter of the folk ballad drowns when she trips into the water while tending ducklings.

clue.text: Role one may play in the marriage market

definitions.text: Role one may play in the marriage market

parts.words: Role one may play in the marriage market
parts.note: a part one, or ..., sounds like casting, but means an eligible match sought by those looking to marry

explanation.walkthrough: The French word for a good match in marriage, someone eligible by wealth or rank; the clue also hints at PART (role) plus I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A parti is a person considered a desirable match because of fortune or status.

clue.text: Mythical party leader in trouble with this gland?

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leader, or first letter, of party is P

explanation.surface: A legendary political leader runs into difficulty, perhaps because of a gland problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges MYTHICAL plus P, the first letter of 'party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lymphatic glands are the lymph nodes of the body's immune drainage system.

clue.text: Inner anguish as part of Hamlet's human heritage

parts.note: the heart stands for one's inner feelings
ache means pain or anguish

explanation.surface: Deep emotional pain is part of what Hamlet sees as humanity's lot.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'To be or not to be' Hamlet speaks of 'the heartache and the thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to', hence heritage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet lists emotional pain among the natural shocks that flesh is heir to, so it is part of mankind's inheritance.

clue.text: Seed supplier carried on dreadfully

indicators.note: done dreadfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A seed merchant behaved appallingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seed supplier' sounds like a merchant; it is a plant whose seeds are used as a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb's dried seeds are a common spice, so the plant supplies seed.

clue.text: His work cut out collecting revenue?

definitions.text: His work cut out collecting revenue?

parts.words: His work cut out collecting revenue?
parts.note: having one's work cut out means a hard task; here the work is excise, a word that also means to cut out

explanation.walkthrough: The old customs officer collected excise duty, and 'excise' as a verb means cut out, so the idiom is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was an officer who collected duties on goods such as alcohol and tobacco.

clue.text: Drug dealer military intelligence put in the box

indicators.note: military intelligence is put in the box, inside it

parts.note: a chest is a large box
MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5

explanation.surface: A drug pusher is boxed in by army spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' suggests a criminal; it is the pharmacist, or chemist in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist who sells medicines.

clue.text: "To what green ——" was Keats's priest leading the heifer?

definitions.text: To what green ——" was Keats's priest leading the heifer?

parts.words: To what green ——" was Keats's priest leading the heifer?
parts.note: a quotation from Ode on a Grecian Urn, which asks where the priest leads a lowing heifer for sacrifice

explanation.walkthrough: Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn asks 'To what green altar, O mysterious priest, / Lead'st thou that heifer lowing at the skies'; the blank is the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrificial heifer is brought to the raised table of an outdoor shrine, the place of offering.

clue.text: His beloved soldier no end distressed

definitions.text: His beloved soldier no end distressed

parts.words: His beloved soldier no end distressed
parts.note: soldier minus its end, rearranged, spells the name of the woman this man loved, so the clue names him through her

explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging SOLDIE (soldier without its last letter) gives ISOLDE; the answer is the knight whose beloved she was.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arthurian legend and Wagner's opera, the Cornish knight loves the Irish princess Isolde.

clue.text: Hodge captures heart of the bird

indicators.note: the farm labourer captures a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Hodge is a traditional English name for a typical farm labourer or rustic

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A countryman catches the bird's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: HODGE is an old nickname for an English farm labourer, so a peasant; 'heart of' takes H, the middle of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird.

clue.text: Mixed-up type goes to church: for a bit

parts.note: pie (also spelt pi) is printers' type that has been spilt and jumbled together
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A muddled sort of person goes to church for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE is a printer's term for type that has been spilt and mixed up; 'goes to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment, a bit of something.

clue.text: Number prepared for orchestra

parts.note: number is both a figure and a musical item; written out for players it is the full music

explanation.walkthrough: The word is also the number twenty, so 'Number' points both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written music for an orchestral piece, and also means twenty.

clue.text: Divine scourge of the fifth century

definitions.text: Divine scourge of the fifth century

parts.words: Divine scourge of the fifth century
parts.note: the Hun leader of the 400s was known as Flagellum Dei, the Scourge of God

explanation.walkthrough: The king of the Huns, who ravaged Europe in the 5th century AD, was called the Scourge of God.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hun king who invaded the Roman Empire in the 440s was nicknamed the Scourge of God.

clue.text: Iris's standard set

definitions.meaning: a flat paving stone, also called a set or sett

explanation.definitionFit: The word names an iris plant, a banner, and a flat paving stone like a sett.

clue.text: As leader I ride a lot, anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any way at all, so the letters may be put in any order

explanation.surface: In charge, I go riding frequently regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' is a newspaper's main opinion article, not a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the main opinion article, also called a leading article.

clue.text: Alluded to it in last month's return

indicators.note: it goes in the abbreviation, placed inside it
a return goes back, so the month's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: December, the year's last month, is abbreviated Dec

explanation.surface: Someone referred to it in a report filed last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns DEC into CED, and 'in' places IT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to refer or mention it as an example or authority.

clue.text: Last term seen cavorting in the river

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits in the river, inside its name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a favourite crossword river

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: At the end of the school term, people were seen frolicking in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' turns TERM into TREM, which goes inside EXE, a river in Devon in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme can mean furthest or final, as in the extreme end of a line.

clue.text: Ruth in the field of Boaz, getting finally not so fat

definitions.text: Ruth in the field of Boaz

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word getting

parts.note: leaner means thinner, less fat

explanation.surface: Biblical Ruth, working in Boaz's field, at last slims down.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth she gathers leftover grain in Boaz's field, which is what a gleaner does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth picked up the barley left behind by harvesters, the work of collecting stray grain after reaping.
